title: 0.7.0 pre-tag checklist and release gate
description:
The durable home for lore-cli's 0.7.0 pre-tag checklist. It exists because on 2026-09-14 that list
lived ONLY in cross-session messages to an orchestrator that was about to be cleared -- which is not
a record, it is a conversation. Anything that fires ON a tag, or that is cheaper to fix before one
than after, belongs here as it is found.

0.7.0 is a PAIR release with quest 0.7.0. The two version numbers move in lockstep from 0.5.0 and
must match before either tags. Campaign is OPAG-142 on opum-agent.

=== THE GATE, per the user via opum-agent, 2026-09-14 ===

Nothing publishes until the backlogs are complete AND all E2E testing is done. opum-cli-e2e is
building a true project-based E2E test at the level a real integration consumer drives the products
(their TASK-62, a Quest-backed project-lifecycle suite), and the pair does not ship until that
qualifies it. The feature burndown is the long pole, not the publish mechanics.

PUBLISH ROUTE IS SETTLED AND IS NOT A BLOCKER: 0.7.0 publishes MANUALLY, same as 0.6.2. LCLI-482
(OIDC trusted publishing broken by GitHub immutable subject claims) is explicitly NOT a release
blocker for 0.7.0 -- it and OPAG-127 stay open for the release AFTER this one, coordinated by the
orchestrator. Do not plan around it and do not attempt the fix as part of this release.

=== CHECKLIST ===

1. LCLI-494 -- FIX IT BEFORE THE TAG, NOT AFTER. This is the item with a real deadline rather than a
   preference. Projection schema 1.1 is on main but NOT YET PUBLISHED, so correcting
   `sourceAdapterVersion` (which claims "backlog-json/1" on Quest-backed exports) now makes the
   correction part of 1.1's definition and no consumer ever sees the intermediate state. After the
   tag, 1.1 has shipped with the field lying and the fix needs its own 1.2 plus a compatibility
   story for records 0.7.0 itself emitted. Same work, materially cheaper before. See LCLI-494's own
   sizing note.

2. LCLI-469 -- notify opum-marketplace of the new tag so it re-resolves the federated skills/ SHA.
   FIRES ON THE TAG. Decide it before tagging, not after.

3. THE NPM TOKEN. It was exposed in a transcript on 2026-09-14 and the user deferred rotation to
   "the next release window" -- 0.7.0 IS that window, and the manual publish path uses it. NOT a
   lore-cli decision: this is the user's, directly. It belongs on this list so it is remembered
   before the publish rather than discovered during it.

4. VERSION BUMP ACROSS THE FAMILY -- package.json plus the six npm/<platform>/package.json manifests,
   and CHANGELOG's `## [Unreleased]` promoted to `## [0.7.0] - <date>`.

5. THE PROVENANCE WARNING MUST BE REPEATED. 0.6.2's changelog entry explains that it ships with NO
   provenance attestation because a manual publish cannot mint one. 0.7.0 publishes manually too, so
   its entry needs the same warning. Do not let the absence read as tampering.

6. RE-ASK QUEST-CLI FOR PRE-TAG ITEMS IMMEDIATELY BEFORE TAGGING, not once during planning
   (quest-cli's own suggestion, 2026-09-14). They had nothing in the "wrong today, expensive after
   0.7.0 ships" category at the time of asking, but QCLI-284/287 were still landing and could
   surface something. The window closes for both repos at the same moment.

7. THE PROSE-DETECTION GAP, carried from LCLI-479. Nothing in this repo verifies that a command named
   in documentation actually exists -- which is how `lore manifest --json` reached a shipped changelog
   entry and LCLI-479's own acceptance criteria past three reviews (there is no such command; it is
   `lore help --json`). test/help.test.ts's manifest/router lockstep guard covers only the opposite
   direction: every manifest command dispatches. A docs-name-a-real-command check is small and would
   have caught it. Not a tag blocker -- listed so it is a decision rather than an omission.

=== WHAT IS ALREADY DONE FOR 0.7.0 ===

LCLI-479 (required flags in help and the machine manifest), LCLI-476 (dependency edges reach
projections/traversal/export, schema 1.1), LCLI-492 (lore sync --fail-on-drop). All on main at
44303b8f.

STILL OPEN IN THE FEATURE BURNDOWN: LCLI-477 (typed authored relationships -- deliberately unstarted,
it is the most design-shaped of the five and should be begun fresh), LCLI-478 (hard maxTokens budget
plus exact-read; BLOCKED on the shared shape with quest's QCLI-276 -- quest has recorded their half as
DEC-3 and lore owes a matching record). Also open: LCLI-494, LCLI-495, LCLI-491 (Ladybug flake).

=== THE RELEASE'S OWN FRAMING, agreed with quest-cli and adopted by opum-agent ===

"0.7.0 makes the graph and the contract legible to an agent, not just to a reader."
Shared principle: "anything an agent parses must be able to express what it does not currently say."
And the line worth using in the notes: we found the defect in ourselves in the same week we named it
-- LCLI-476 alone turned up two hard-coded version literals where a constant belonged, neither
tested, one of which announced a schema version it did not emit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: LCLI-494 is resolved BEFORE the tag, or a deliberate decision is recorded here to let it ship wrong and correct it in 1.2 — not left to be discovered after tagging.
LCLI-469 is decided before the tag, since it fires ON the tag (opum-marketplace re-resolves the federated skills/ SHA).
The npm token question is put to the USER directly before the publish — not to the orchestrator, and not discovered during it.
Version numbers match quest 0.7.0 exactly, bumped across package.json and all six npm/<platform> manifests, with CHANGELOG [Unreleased] promoted to [0.7.0] and dated.
0.7.0`s changelog entry repeats the no-provenance-attestation warning, since it publishes manually like 0.6.2 and an absent attestation must not read as tampering.
quest-cli is re-asked for pre-tag items immediately before tagging, not only during planning.
The release gate is satisfied: the feature backlog is complete AND opum-cli-e2e`s project-based E2E qualification has passed against the pair.

implementationNotes:
CHECKLIST ITEM 1 IS DONE, AND THE DEADLINE IT CARRIED IS MET. LCLI-494 landed as PR #80 on dev at 66a296ac, BEFORE any 0.7.0 tag. `sourceAdapterVersion` is now threaded from the producing adapter, so projection schema 1.1 will ship with the field correct from its first published moment and no consumer ever sees the intermediate state. The expensive branch this item existed to avoid -- 1.1 shipping with the field lying, then a 1.2 plus a compatibility story for records 0.7.0 itself emitted -- is closed.

THE 0.7.0 FEATURE BURNDOWN IS COMPLETE ON LORE'S SIDE. Delivered since this checklist was written, all merged to dev:

  LCLI-477 (#76) typed authored relationships and claim state, ADR-0021
  LCLI-478 (#77 record, #79 implementation) hard maxTokens ceiling and `lore read`
  LCLI-494 (#80) sourceAdapterVersion names the producing adapter
  LCLI-497 (#75) indexed backend repaired -- a release blocker found mid-campaign
  LCLI-498 (#81) fallback advisory names its cause, and every route announces itself
  LCLI-499 (#78) every retrieval-family command reports `data.backend`

THREE OF THOSE SIX WERE NOT ON THE ORIGINAL LIST and are worth naming, because the checklist should record what a burndown actually costs. 497 was a regression LCLI-476 introduced and nobody detected -- found by accident three hours later. 499 and 498 are its detectors: nothing a consumer could read said which backend served a request, and the one advisory that existed fired on some fallback routes and not others. A fix without its detector is a promise the same defect will be found by accident next time.

WHAT THE REMAINING ITEMS NEED, none of which is lore implementation work:

  2. LCLI-469 -- still open, still fires ON the tag. Unchanged.
  3. The npm token question goes to the USER directly, before the publish.
  4. Version bump across package.json and the six npm/<platform> manifests, CHANGELOG [Unreleased] -> [0.7.0] dated, matching quest 0.7.0 exactly.
  5. The no-provenance-attestation warning repeated in 0.7.0's entry.
  6. quest-cli re-asked for pre-tag items immediately before tagging.
  7. The gate: backlogs complete AND opum-cli-e2e's project-based qualification passed against the PAIR.

ON ITEM 7, AND IT IS A REAL DEPENDENCY RATHER THAN A FORMALITY: opum-cli-e2e's TASK-64 gates on both packages resolving at 0.7.0 ON NPM, not on a dev merge. So their qualification cannot run before the publish it is meant to gate, and the sequencing has to be decided rather than assumed. They also hold one BLOCKED row waiting on `--edge dependency`, which is data-dependent rather than version-gated -- their fixture needs a task with a prerequisite -- and one row asserting the ABSENCE of a backend field, which LCLI-499 has now made assertable positively. Both were routed to them with the shape attached.

LCLI-491 (ladybug concurrency flake) is untouched and stays that way: its timeout must not be raised before the distribution is measured.

SESSION HANDOFF, 2026-09-15. Written on this task because nothing is In Progress and this is the durable record of what remains before the 0.7.0 tag. The flush hook writes a tracker note only when exactly one task is In Progress, so it will correctly write none; this note is the part it cannot do.

=== THREE CORRECTIONS TO A STALE BRIEF, verified against live state ===

The recycled orchestrator's handoff brief cited three facts that are no longer true. Recorded here rather than only in message traffic, because the next reader may be handed the same stale brief.

1. "dev is +6 vs main and unpromoted" -- NO. dev was promoted and main is identical to it.
     origin/main: 60fb43b4f5754b932414486ce393d41b5723124a
     origin/dev:  60fb43b4f5754b932414486ce393d41b5723124a
     git rev-list --count origin/main..origin/dev -> 0
   The promotion was approved by the previous orchestrator instance, which verified the fast-forward independently before granting it (PR #84, auto-marked MERGED, no merge commit). Post-push assertions verified: identical SHAs, empty `git diff --stat origin/main origin/dev`, `merge-base --is-ancestor` holds.

2. "LCLI-498 is the next and last pre-tag item" -- NO. LCLI-498 is DONE, delivered in PR #81 and merged to dev, then promoted. So is LCLI-499 (PR #78). Neither is outstanding.

3. "close or annotate any In Progress task" -- there are none. `quest task list --status "In Progress"` is empty, and the working tree is clean.

THE ONE PREMISE THAT WAS CORRECT is LCLI-491, and it is carried below unchanged.

=== STANDING INSTRUCTIONS, recorded as asked ===

LCLI-491 -- DO NOT RAISE THE LADYBUG TIMEOUT before the real distribution is measured. The projection-lifecycle test times out at 5000ms intermittently; raising the bound without measuring how long it actually takes converts a flake into a slower flake and destroys the evidence needed to fix it. Untouched by this campaign and to stay that way.

LCLI-498 AND LCLI-499 ARE SEPARATE ON PURPOSE, and both records already say so from their own side -- so a reader arriving at either finds the reasoning without needing the other. 499's summary: "Warn on every fallback" and "report the backend on every response" are different fixes; only the second was ruled in. 498's summary: making the previously-silent fallback route warn belongs WITH the naming-the-cause work, because "the advisory names its cause" and "the advisory is emitted" are one defect from two angles, and shipping the first alone gives a warning that names its cause except when there is none. opum-agent left that call to this repository and confirmed it afterwards.

=== WHAT THE 0.7.0 GATE STILL NEEDS, none of it lore implementation ===

Checklist items 2-7 on this task, unchanged: LCLI-469 (fires ON the tag), the npm token question which goes to the USER directly, the version bump across package.json and the six npm/<platform> manifests with CHANGELOG [Unreleased] -> [0.7.0] dated to match quest 0.7.0 exactly, the no-provenance-attestation warning repeated, and quest-cli re-asked for pre-tag items immediately before tagging.

AND THE UNRESOLVED SEQUENCING PROBLEM, which is a decision and not a task: the user's instruction is that nothing publishes until the backlogs are complete AND all E2E testing is done, but opum-cli-e2e's qualification resolves both packages from npm at 0.7.0 -- so it cannot run before the publish it is meant to gate. The instruction as given has no satisfiable ordering. opum-agent took it to the user rather than ruling, which is right: the step it collides on is the one they reserved. Do not pick an ordering silently.

The two shapes, so whoever picks this up does not re-derive them: qualifying pre-publish means qualifying against something other than the published artifact, which weakens it to roughly what CI already proves; publishing first means the gate becomes a rollback trigger rather than a gate. Different guarantees, neither obviously right -- it turns on whether "all E2E testing done" means "before anyone can install it" or "before we tell anyone to".

=== FOR THE NEXT SESSION ===

Skills to reach for: `opum-sdlc` before any branch or PR, `opum-handoff` on restart, `opum-lore:lore` for anything under docs/. Run `quest instructions overview` first, per CLAUDE.md.

Repo state at handoff, all verified rather than remembered: dev == main == 60fb43b4, working tree clean, no stray branches, nothing In Progress, `bun test` 3048 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, `lore check` 78 files 0 errors 0 warnings, `quest doctor` healthy.

There is no outstanding implementation work. Everything remaining is gated on the publish or owned by someone else.
